summary: In major space policy developments, President Trump has signed a new national space policy aimed at enabling 1,000 U.S. rocket launches per year and announced that NASA’s Artemis II crew will receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor. On the military front, U.S. Space Command is relocating 200 personnel to Alabama this year while preparing for ground-segment defenses and cislunar operations, a U.S. Air Force flight to Antarctica was forced to turn back following a warning about hazardous Russian space activity, and a new White House strategy highlighted outer space, undersea systems, and artificial intelligence as top military priorities. In commercial launch and industry, SpaceX performed a static fire of Starship ahead of its first orbital test flight and successfully launched 29 Starlink satellites on a separate mission, while Muon Space raised $250 million in Series C funding as new industry forecasts predict more than 6,500 Earth observation satellites will launch by 2035. In astronomical science, observations from the James Webb Space Telescope revealed hidden stars showing that the universe's earliest galaxies were much larger than previously understood. Internationally, China is preparing to launch its Chang'e 7 moon probe to search for lunar water ice in one of its most ambitious missions to date. Looking ahead, readers should watch for Japan's space agency to launch its dedicated Mars moon sample-return spacecraft on October 19.
